newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-DLR TO CONSOLIDATE BEFORE RESUMING UPTREND.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-DLR TO CONSOLIDATE BEFORE RESUMING UPTREND.

text.p: Technicians expect the dollar to consolidate in a new, lower range in the coming days, perhaps testing Friday's troughs before resuming its upward trend against the mark and yen.

"There's a slight chance we could extend a little bit on the downside," said Pete Grant, senior technical foreign exchange analyst at MMS International. "But I'm still viewing the last several days of losses as corrective within the longer term uptrend."
Initial support in dollar/yen was pegged at 115.00 with a stronger prop at Friday's low of 114.25.
In dollar/mark, last week's lows of 1.8380/90 should cap the downside, although a close below 1.8400 could open the door for a brief venture into the 1.82s, chartists predicted.

Beyond there, however, the damage should be limited. The dollar's upside appears equally contained, with strong resistance coming in near 1.8650 marks -- a congestion area and 50 percent retracement of the move from the rate's recent high of 1.8913 to Friday's low.
Ahead of that key level, technicians were expecting active selling by short-term traders in the days ahead.

"If you're a short-term trader I think you take a shot at selling the rallies," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America. "I think dollar/mark will be choppy in a trading range before we go back up."
At 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, the dollar was changing hands near its session peak at 1.8612/17 marks and fetching 116.03/08 yen.
"After a week of consolidation I think we'll start edging higher again and get back on track for 1.90-plus marks," said Grant.
